strengths: The concept of interactive, region-aware reasoning (hypothesize, crop/zoom, and verify) is highly novel and intuitive for Image Quality Assessment (IQA), mimicking human cognitive behavior when evaluating complex visual artifacts.

The curation of the Grounded-Rationale-IQA (GR-IQA) dataset is technically sound, employing clever mechanisms like Visual Reliance Filtering (VRF) and Hint-Augmented Consistency Filtering (HACF) to strictly prevent LLM/VLM hallucinations.

The proposed KL-Coverage regularizer successfully addresses the common RL 'score collapse' or entropy collapse issue on numerical tokens, leading to a much more realistic and diverse score distribution (as shown by the high unique score ratio on KonIQ).

Comprehensive experiments and ablation studies demonstrate consistent improvements in both quantitative score regression (PLCC/SRCC across 7 datasets) and qualitative reasoning accuracy (via VLM-as-judge).
The applicability of the generated rationales to guide downstream state-of-the-art image restoration models (e.g., SUPIR/DreamClear) is practically demonstrated and visually compelling.
weaknesses: The paper lacks a discussion on computational complexity and latency. Since the proposed method employs multi-turn interaction (cropping/zooming and re-evaluating), it would be beneficial to quantify the average inference latency, computational cost, and token overhead compared to single-pass models like Q-Align or DeQA.

The interactive loop seems to be restricted to a maximum of two turns (one crop operation followed by a final decision). It is not fully clear if the policy can support multiple consecutive zoom operations on even smaller sub-regions, or if it is strictly limited by the prompt template.

The evaluation of downstream image restoration is primarily qualitative. Including quantitative metrics (such as FID, NIQE, or user study preference scores on the restored images) would make the case for Zoom-IQA's real-world utility much stronger.

Some hyperparameter choices, such as the thresholds for VRF (rating difference < 0.05, Bounding Box IoU > 0.5) and the top-p proportion (p = 0.02) for the KL-Coverage mask, are introduced without a sensitivity analysis to show how they affect the model's overall performance.

strengths: Intuitive Cognitive Paradigm: Emulating the human 'zoom-in' behavior for image quality assessment (IQA) is highly logical, mimicking how humans inspect fine-grained details when uncertain.

Rigorous Dataset Curation: The pipeline for building Grounded-Rationale-IQA (GR-IQA) dataset introduces effective filtering mechanisms (Visual Reliance Filtering and Hint-Augmented Consistency Filtering) to mitigate language priors and hallucinations.

Addressing Score/Entropy Collapse: The proposed KL-Coverage regularizer addresses a critical limitation in RL-based VLM training (score collapse), significantly improving the diversity of generated quality scores.

Comprehensive Evaluation: The paper evaluates the model thoroughly across seven benchmark datasets for score regression, employs VLMs as judges to quantitatively rate description quality, and successfully demonstrates the benefit of the generated rationales in downstream image restoration.
weaknesses: Computational Efficiency: The multi-turn zoom-and-crop mechanism naturally increases the inference cost and latency. An analysis showing the average number of turns, computational overhead, or latency comparison against single-pass VLMs is missing.

Fair Baseline Comparison: The model is built on Qwen2.5-VL-7B. It is unclear if the performance gains over prior works (like Q-Insight or VisualQuality-R1) are partially due to the stronger base model. An ablation or comparison using the same base model for competing methods would strengthen the claims.

strengths: An innovative interactive "hypothesize-ground-verify" (crop-and-zoom) framework for no-reference image quality assessment (IQA), mirroring how humans inspect images.

Curation of a high-fidelity Grounded-Rationale-IQA (GR-IQA) dataset with novel filters like Visual Reliance Filtering (VRF) and Hint-Augmented Consistency Filtering (HACF) to eliminate language priors and hallucinations.
Introduction of a KL-Coverage regularizer that successfully addresses the "score collapse" problem common in RL-trained VLMs, preserving the continuous nature of IQA score predictions.
Strong experimental validation across seven diverse benchmarks, outperforming recent reasoning-based IQA models like Q-Insight and VisualQuality-R1.
A practical downstream demonstration showing that the generated textual rationales can guide modern generative restoration models (DreamClear) to achieve superior perceptual results.
weaknesses: The multi-turn iterative nature of the model (using Qwen2.5-VL-7B for multiple passes during zoom-in) introduces considerable computational overhead and inference latency compared to single-pass VLM-IQA methods.

The data curation pipeline relies heavily on high-end closed-source models (Gemini-2.5-Pro), which might limit the accessibility and easy reproduction of the dataset curation process for resource-constrained researchers.
A quantitative discussion regarding the exact token budget, average number of turns/crops per image, and exact inference runtime is currently missing.

strengths: Introduction of a novel interactive paradigm for Image Quality Assessment (IQA) that emulates human cognitive behavior of 'cropping and zooming' to resolve local uncertainties.

A rigorous dataset curation pipeline (GR-IQA) that incorporates Visual Reliance Filtering (VRF) and Hint-Augmented Consistency Filtering (HACF) to significantly reduce hallucinations and ensure strong visual grounding of rationales.
The proposed KL-Coverage Regularizer successfully addresses the 'score collapse' (or policy entropy drop) problem typical in RL-based IQA, preserving score and reasoning diversity.

Thorough evaluation on seven standard IQA benchmarks, coupled with validation on visual quality description (via VLM-as-judge and human evaluations) and downstream text-guided image restoration tasks (SUPIR, DreamClear).
weaknesses: Increased computational and token overhead: The interactive multi-turn pipeline (first-turn hypothesis followed by cropping and second-turn verification) inevitably increases token consumption and computation time compared to single-pass models, which might limit deployment on edge devices.

High dependency on powerful closed-source models (Gemini-2.5-Pro) and large LLMs (Qwen-2.5-32b) for data synthesis and verification, which poses reproducibility challenges for academic labs with restricted resources.

The pure scoring accuracy (PLCC/SRCC in Table 1) occasionally lags behind some state-of-the-art non-reasoning score-based VLM methods (such as DeQA-Score), suggesting a minor trade-off between generating explanations/grounding and optimizing solely for regression metrics.

strengths: Highly intuitive and novel cognitive paradigm (hypothesize-verify via cropping/zooming) to address the lack of physical visual grounding and unreliable text-only reasoning in VLM-based IQA models.
A well-structured and theoretically sound two-stage training pipeline: stage 1 (SFT) teaches the model 'how' to crop, while stage 2 (RL) teaches the model 'when' to crop via a dynamic policy.

Meticulous dataset curation pipeline for Grounded-Rationale-IQA (GR-IQA) employing Visual Reliance Filtering (VRF) and Hint-Augmented Consistency Filtering (HACF), effectively suppressing VLM hallucinations and language prior bias.
An elegant solution (KL-Coverage Regularizer) targeting the entropy/score collapse problem of RL in numerical-token generation tasks.
Impressive downstream utility demonstrated on text-guided image restoration models (SUPIR and DreamClear), showing both quantitative improvements and superior visual quality.
Thorough experiments across seven benchmarks with extensive ablation studies, cross-dataset evaluations, VLM-as-judge benchmarks, and human user studies.
weaknesses: Increased computational complexity and latency: the dynamic multi-turn visual loop requires cropping operations and multiple forward passes through the VLM, which makes it less ideal for high-throughput, real-time application scenarios.

The dataset curation, filtering, and evaluation pipelines heavily depend on advanced, proprietary, or massive models (such as Gemini-2.5-pro, Qwen-2.5-32b, and GPT-5-mini), which may pose long-term reproducibility and accessibility challenges.

The current framework is constrained to a single zoom-in action per image. For complex images featuring heterogeneous or spatially distributed degradation types, a multi-turn, multi-region zoom mechanism might be needed but is not currently supported.

strengths: The concept of interactive 'crop-and-zoom' for vision-language model (VLM) based image quality assessment (IQA) is highly novel and successfully mimics the human visual inspection process of zooming in on key details.

The curated Grounded-Rationale-IQA (GR-IQA) dataset is carefully constructed with rigorous verification pipelines, namely Visual Reliance Filtering (VRF) and Hint-Augmented Consistency Filtering (HACF), to prevent visual-textual hallucinations.

The reinforcement learning phase introduces effective stabilizers, such as the KL-Coverage regularizer to address the issue of policy entropy/score collapse, and a Progressive Re-sampling Strategy to mitigate data imbalance.

Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that the model generates highly precise, region-grounded descriptions that improve VLM-as-judge scores and can be effectively used to guide downstream generative image restoration tasks.
weaknesses: The proposed method is computationally and conceptually complex, requiring a multi-stage training pipeline (SFT followed by GRPO reinforcement learning) and multiple heavy models (Gemini-2.5-pro and Qwen-2.5-32b) for dataset curation.
The iterative nature of the 'crop-and-zoom' mechanism inevitably increases the inference latency and computational footprint due to multiple forward passes of the 7B visual-language model.

While the model significantly outperforms other reasoning-based VLM baselines, there remains a slight performance gap in raw correlation scores (PLCC/SRCC) on a few benchmarks (e.g., KonIQ and Live-Wild) compared to pure, score-only VLM regressors such as DeQA-Score.
